utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, we are in open session. The voice distortion is now on. I'm asked to remind everybody that when the voice distortion is on, they should switch their microphones off when they're not speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm not finished with the meeting which we were dealing with in private session. Could I ask that we -- or it may make sense just to conclude that portion of B-1237's testimony and then go into open session or however the Chamber would like to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I apologise for taking your testimony somewhat out of order. We are now in open session, and I'd ask you just to give us briefly some basic background facts about Zvornik. Approximately how many people were living in Zvornik at the end of 1991 and the beginning of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zvornik is one of the municipalities which is on the very border between Bosnia and Serbia, on the banks of the Drina River. The municipality itself had about 80.000 inhabitants, and the town of Zvornik itself about 20.000 inhabitants. The ethnic composition was mostly as follows: 60 per cent of the population were Muslims, about 38 per cent were Serbs, and there were 2 per cent others, mostly a couple of Croatian families, a couple of Jewish families, a couple of Romany settlements too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it true that at the end of 1991 and the beginning of 1992 that the relationship between the Serb community and the Muslim community began to deteriorate, and was this in your mind marked in particularity by a comment you heard Branko Grujic make at a meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is true that relations deteriorated, inter-ethnic relations, that is, and it is true that I heard certain comments by Mr. Branko Grujic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please summarise the comments that you heard Mr. Grujic say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said, "You Muslims must understand that we don't want to live with you. One of the reasons is, for instance, the way in which you're exploiting the Serbs. You're multiplying, that is, Muslims are multiplying more quickly than Serbs, and our children go to joint schools and joint kindergartens which are financed out of joint funds. In this way, we are paying for the maintenance and schooling of your children, and we won't go on doing that."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Who was this Mr. Grujic? If we've had evidence, I don't recollect that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please remind us who Mr. Grujic was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic was president of the Party of Democratic Action in Veliki Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 441, tab 2. And this can be placed on the overhead projector. Sir, do you recognise this exhibit? You can look at the actual exhibit to your left.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do know this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do you recognise it to be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is actually a review, an overview, of names, first and last, indicating titles of the gentlemen I came across in that period of time that I communicated with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you involved in the creation of this document and have you checked it for its accuracy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I have verified the accuracy of this document, and I have signed it as being accurate and authentic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I ask that it be left on the overhead projector so we can refer to it during the course of the testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, I want to now draw your attention to the period between January and March of 1992. During that time period, did you become aware that parallel governmental structures were being established by the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I learnt about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask you to describe the structures or organisations that you have personal knowledge of and explain how you knew that these structures were being established.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A Serbian municipality of Zvornik was set up, a Serbian SUP, a Serbian Territorial Defence was formed. The way in which these were formed was as follows: The Serbs simply withdrew from all the municipal bodies based in town of Zvornik, and they set up premises in companies in Karakaj. They stole a couple of passenger vehicles, including the car of the president of the municipality, and they simply no longer appeared at official meetings of the Municipal Assembly. This escalated, in particular, in March, even though obstruction started already at the end of 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention to February of 1992. During this time period, did you become aware of the movement of JNA military resources in and around the Municipality of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I learnt about the movement and presence of the Yugoslav People's Army in and around the municipality of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a person by the name of -- are you aware of a person by the name of Colonel Tacic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I did know that person by the name of Colonel Tacic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what unit he commanded and what movement of that unit you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was in command of an armoured brigade which, until the outbreak of the conflict with Croatia, was stationed in Jastrebarsko in the vicinity of Zagreb. And at the beginning of February, it was dislocated or moved to Dubrave, which was in the vicinity of Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did his unit once again move to the area of Mali Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. As tensions grew, it became clearer and clearer what the real purpose of that unit was, and in end March, that unit occupied all the bridges in Zvornik municipality, and a couple of tanks were deployed in Mali Zvornik itself with their barrels trained towards my place of birth, my home village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I will ask you about the presence of paramilitary forces in Zvornik a little later in your testimony, but at this stage, the time that you're describing as each of the bridges being secured by these JNA resources, as you've described, were there any paramilitary forces from Serbia in Zvornik prior to the securing of the bridges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were no paramilitaries in Zvornik before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask now that the witness be shown a copy of a map from Prosecution Exhibit 336, pages 28 and 29. I'm going to ask it be placed on the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you to take the pointer. I will ask you a few questions about this map. My first question to you is: Is it you that made the markings on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do the markings on the map indicate? Please don't give us the location now but tell us what do they generally indicate, these circles you've made on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They indicate the places where the forces of Colonel Tacic were deployed and the forces of the Serbian Territorial Defence of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask you to go through each of the locations, point to it, "A" through "E" and just tell us the locations where you have knowledge that these forces were so deployed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Location "A" indicates this place, Dubrava, where the staff was initially located. I mean, the staff of Colonel Tacic. Location "B" is Sekovici, the place where in the course of March Colonel Tacic deployed his forces. And the same goes for location "C", Papraca village, where in end March the new staff of Colonel Tacic was dislocated. Point "D" is, in fact, Mali Zvornik. The place of deployment of this armoured brigade and the forces of Colonel Tacic and the Territorial Defence of Mali Zvornik. Celopek and Trsic are places where the forces of Colonel Tacic were deployed together with the Serbian Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do we have a number for this brigade or a name? Can you help us with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was simply an armoured mechanised brigade from Jastrebarsko. That's how we referred to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the troops that you're describing now, were they deployed in a way, a secret way, or were they visible to people that would have been in the area, in the areas you've described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were visible in these areas that I just described. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you to summarise the types of military resources, to the extent you haven't already, that you personally observed, the types of equipment and also the quantity of men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw tanks and anti-aircraft cannons that were deployed at every bridge, and in Mali Zvornik, in Celopek, Trsic, and at the hydro power station of Mali Zvornik. In Dubrava, I saw similar weapons as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to return briefly to the bridges that you described as being secured. Could I ask you to name the bridges and the locations where those bridges are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first bridge is the so-called new bridge in Zvornik, a concrete bridge located in Zvornik's industrial area. The second bridge is the railroad bridge which connects the industrial area of Zvornik with Serbia. And a third bridge is the bridge at Sepak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the course of your testimony, you've referred to both Colonel Tacic and Captain Obrenovic. My question to you is: What if anything do you know about the relationship, the command relationship, between those two men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, if Colonel Tacic was the commander, the superior of Captain Obrenovic, then Captain Obrenovic was commanding only a part of that brigade, a smaller part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where Captain Obrenovic was based from? Where was his base of operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He mainly covered Karakaj, Celopek, and Mali Zvornik and moved within that circle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the name General Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with that name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who he was and what was his command relationship to Colonel Tacic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: General Jankovic was the commander of that military district of Tuzla, and he was superior to Colonel Tacic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A few days prior to the attack on Zvornik, were you present at a lunch where several people were, including General Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please describe what occurred at that lunch? And I'd ask you to begin by telling us to the best of your recollection where it was and when it was?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you summarise the relevant portions of that luncheon meeting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was a very pleasant luncheon for the most part. General Jankovic did most of the talking. He was a very witty gentleman, the soul of the party. He told us jokes about his own folks, Montenegrin men and women. He tried to calm us down. He told us that there was no reason for us to be afraid, that the army would not attack us. On the contrary, they would protect our people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention now to early April. Can you describe how the situation developed in early April and whether or not there was a Muslim crisis committee was established during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the situation in Zvornik was very, very tense. There had been a couple of murders, assassinations in Kravica, that is Bratunac municipality. Then there had been the murder of a policeman in Kalesija. The SUP had already been disbanded. In fact, Serb members had established their own parallel SUP. The Serb Territorial Defence had been set up, the Serb Municipal Assembly. And from the old town itself, Serbs continued to move out. And a couple of days prior to the attack on Zvornik, there was not a single Serb there. The Crisis Staff was set up on the 6th of April when it was already certain and perfectly clear what was in the offing. And the purpose of creating that Crisis Staff and the purpose of all its activities was to avoid war at all costs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to now draw your attention to the 7th of April, 1992. Did you become aware that a number of men from or associated with Arkan were arrested or detained in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did learn about that, that a group of Arkan's men had been taken into custody into the SUP building of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us how you knew that these men were taken into custody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, at that moment, I was on duty at the SUP according to the schedule that the Crisis Staff had made on the 6th of April, and I was there when a group of citizens brought in four members of Arkan's paramilitary units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were. They had Magnum pistols. They had knives. They had handcuffs that the police force was equipped with at the time, and they had wires for strangling people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where precisely were they detained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were arrested at the crossing from Karakaj, that is the Serbian part of the municipality of Zvornik, at the entrance to Vidak's field, which is the Muslim part of Zvornik. And they said they were on their way to the Jezero Hotel, according to instructions from Belgrade. It was the location where they were supposed to join their units and move into the action of liberating Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Excuse me. Could I ask the usher to hand a note to the registrar. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that these men were detained, were the bridges that you've described earlier as being secured by the JNA, were they still secured in that fashion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They were still secured in the same way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the men that were detained, did they have identification cards with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did have IDs, and these IDs were signed by Arkan, his full name, as well as the emblem of the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you a question about the border controls. When people would pass from Zvornik into Mali Zvornik and vice versa, would they be asked to produce identification to identify themselves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In addition to the fact that the situation was still very tense, in fact even though the situation was very tense, crossings were still possible, although the police did check every person and every car that came into Zvornik. The other bridges, the railroad bridge and the concrete bridge in Karakaj, were completely inaccessible, and fishermen could not cross them at all. They chased them away. And every access to Zvornik was under strict control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the men make statements regarding where they were trying to go at the time they were detained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The shortest one among them who had a pony-tail said that the Belgrade media, radio and television, incessantly broadcast reports about the corpses of Serbs flowing down the Drina River, about camps that had been set up at football stadiums in Muslim areas, and that every Serb should help to save Serbs in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they make any statements regarding the presence of other like people in Mali Zvornik, Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They said their unit was waiting for them there, and it was their assembly point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at the time that these men described what they were hearing in the media in Belgrade, had any of that or did you make any observations that would have formed a basis for that? Did you see any bodies in the Drina or did you see or know of the existence of any detention centres for Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I neither noticed anything, nor did it exist in the first place in our municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I'm going to move to paragraph 62 of the summary on page 10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can I ask you to tell us, when did -- when did the outbreak of hostilities actually begin in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please clarify your question? What do you mean when you say "hostilities"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when in your view there was an attack on Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The attack occurred in the small hours of the 8th of April. It started with rifle fire from Karakaj against the Muslim areas of Zvornik municipality, which was in fact just an introduction for the general attack, for the all-out attack that followed around 8.00 in the evening of the 8th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you use the word "all-out attack," could I ask you to describe what precisely you mean.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that conversation with that paramilitary unit and after the ultimatum, at 8.00 in the evening bombing started, shelling of the town of Zvornik, mainly its Muslim neighbourhoods known as Zamlaz, Bajr and Fetija, and Vidak's field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you still in the central part or still in Zvornik town itself at the time the shelling began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not. I was on the hills above my village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you estimate for us the quantity of shells that you heard or saw on that evening strike the towns of -- the Muslim areas that you've just described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That night about 200 shells were fired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to see from where those shells were fired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were fired from the territory of Mali Zvornik municipality, or more precisely a location near the mosque in Mali Zvornik, also from Karakaj and Celopek.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you able to tell from where these shells were fired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It was night-time. You see a radiant light from the explosion of shells and the trace of them falling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did the local Territorial Defence unit of Mali Zvornik or of Zvornik itself have the type of equipment necessary to fire the quantity and type of shells that fell on Zvornik that night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It certainly did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the following days, were you able to -- from where you were at this time, able to see some of the events that were transpiring down in the town of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was in a position to see the events in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your viewing of events in Zvornik, was it done with the unassisted eye or did you have anything to amplify and magnify your view?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had my service binoculars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I ask you about specific events that you saw, I would ask you to summarise the general -- your general observations during this time period.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the shelling which took place in the night of the 8th of April, paramilitary units together with the Territorial Defence, the Serb TO of Zvornik, of Mali Zvornik and Loznica municipalities began the ethnic cleansing of the town itself, the town of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "ethnic cleansing," can you please describe your particular observations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the parts of town that are close to the first neighbouring village, I saw them taking out people from residential buildings and private houses. I saw them separating women and children from men and executing grown-up men and even grown children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to now draw your attention to some specific events. Did there come a time when you saw a number of people taken from an apartment block in Zamlaz?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I did see a group of about perhaps ten men, ten people taken out from a residential building in Zamlaz.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when, to the best of your recollection, did you make this observation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw that on the 9th of April. It might have been between 10.00 and 12.00, perhaps 11.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please describe what you saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw them taking people out. I saw them removing women and executing a group of about ten men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to tell from your vantage point whether or not the men that you say were executed were armed at the time of their execution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those people were civilians who were unarmed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to recognise any of the people that were executed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I recognised late Sabit Bilalic and his son whom I can't recall now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you able to recognise those two among the group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sabit was one of the biggest men in Zvornik. He had extremely -- he had an extremely thick moustache. And his son was very tall and played basketball in the first village. I knew them personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you observe another group of ten people taken from this same part of town towards the centre of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe your observations of this group of ten people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw a group that was being taken towards the centre of Zvornik, and I heard volleys of gunfire being fired. I heard moans and screams.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know a person by the name of Fehim Kujundzic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew the late Fehim. He was the director of the secondary technical school in Zvornik. He was a personal friend of mine and a colleague of mine. For a while we worked together at the secondary school in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see or hear anything occur in the vicinity of where he lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw that paramilitary formations were present in front of his building too, and I heard bursts of gunfire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to now draw your attention to Hudovic street. Did you make any observations of events on that street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I saw these same units mercilessly executing a man. Also, I saw them mercilessly killing a person who tried to come up to this man and help him. This happened in the main street in Zvornik at the entrance into Zvornik on the road leading further on to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of the people that you've described as seeing them killed, were any of them armed that you could tell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Nobody was armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your vantage point, were you able to see some activity on one of the bridges that connected Zvornik with Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Across the bridge which is known as the bridge of Filip Kljajic in Zvornik. There was a group of citizens crossing that bridge, women and children primarily. They were going in the direction of Mali Zvornik where a collection centre was, actually, for the deportation of citizens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this time when you could see the bridge, were the JNA -- was the JNA still securing the bridge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That bridge was secured by a MUP unit from Mali Zvornik together with the Yugoslav People's Army, and everybody had to show their IDs when crossing over to the Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The killings that you've described, were you able to identify any of the perpetrators or any of the organisations that they may have belonged to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the perpetrators were primarily members of these paramilitary units. They had camouflage uniforms, officer's boots. They had camouflage caps, camouflage hoods, automatic rifles identical to the weapons and equipment I had seen the day before during the meeting at the Jezero Hotel in Mali Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you estimate what period of time, how many hours, were you making your observations from the vantage point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, a few hours must have gone by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the hours that you were making these observations, did you at any time see members of the Yugoslav People's Army intervene and prevent some of the killings and other things that you've described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't notice anything that would indicate that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would they have been in a similar position as you to see and be aware of what was going on in the town of Zvornik that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were 100 per cent aware of everything that had been going on in Zvornik, and they are the ones who had prepared for everything that had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, it's now for you to cross-examine, bearing in mind that part of the testimony was in private session, and if you want to cross-examine about that, we must go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to take things in order, Mr. May, according to the testimony of this witness, although it was my understanding yesterday that this session was partly closed because the equipment was not working for voice distortion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That was not the reason. So anything that was in private session, cross-examine in private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, then. Then I will first have to ask him about what he testified about in the beginning, because I don't find this very clear. I don't find the reasons or the motives clear, and this entire conduct that is described by the witness. Now, if this has to be in private session, then I will examine him in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you want to go chronologically, you can begin by asking him about events which he described this morning, but there may come a time when you've got to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Mr. May. Any way you want. You can handle it any way you want. I assume these are things that can be referred to in public session because you explained the reasons for private session by being a small number of persons, and this doesn't have to do with this small number of persons. Cross-examined by Mr. Milosevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you can see from the information provided here, you were a member of the leadership in Zvornik; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. That document was introduced under seal, the background document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not specifically say which position he held, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you were a member of the leadership at the time, which you described, does that also mean that you were a member of the Party of Democratic Action? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was never a member of the Party of Democratic Action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The president of the municipality, was he a member of the Party of Democratic Action and a leader of the Party of Democratic Action?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was a member of the Party of Democratic Action and a member of the Executive Board of the Party of Democratic Action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You explained -- you mentioned, rather, the name of Branko Grujic, that he was president of the Serb Democratic Party in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was president of the Party of Democratic Action in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Asim Juzbasic. Dr. Asim Juzbasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you described Grujic as having said that Muslims were exploiting the Serbs, that he said that in some speech of his --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, where did Grujic make this speech?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He made this speech at the meeting hall of the Municipal Assembly of Veliki Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that Grujic, which I assume was then an assemblyman in Veliki Zvornik and a member of the SDS after the elections --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he was a member of the Assembly of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I saw him at all meetings of the assemblies and he was probably an assemblyman, a member of the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he spoke at a session of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it only Grujic who spoke at the Municipal Assembly meeting that you're describing or did this president of yours also make a speech at that Municipal Assembly meeting? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did speak, but about a completely different subject.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that none of you who were present there made any comments whatsoever in respect of what Grujic had said, that the Serbs were -- that the Muslims were exploiting the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I commented on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you take a position then about this? As far as I understand, this was a polemic at the regular meeting of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the position of the Municipal Assembly then about this political polemic of yours as to who was exploiting who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No position was taken. No resolutions were passed, official resolutions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I assume that the president of the Municipal Assembly was chairing the meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The President of the Assembly of Zvornik was a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: His name is not a secret, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I leave it to the Trial Chamber to decide about that. It is well known who the president was. Well, yes, you can say who it was.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot hear the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The interpreters are having some problem hearing you, Mr. Milosevic, so would you speak clearly, please. The registrar explains there's some difficulty about the microphone, but go on. We'll do as best we can. Just try and leave a pause, if you would, Mr. Milosevic, between answer and question and that would assist.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Mr. May, okay now. [Interpretation] From time to time my microphone goes off without me having done anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I know. It's not your responsibility. It's not your responsibility. Now, let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the Municipal Assembly, you had representatives of the SDA and the SDS for the most part; is that right, after these elections?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any officials at the municipality who did not belong to a single party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I was an official who did not belong to any party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there any other such examples?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that I know of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I can see it here on the computer monitor still. You gave a table, a list of persons on this particular table. Mr. Groome said that this was some kind of a document. I understood on the basis of your statement that it is their officials who made a table of persons that you refer to in your statement and that that table was made or, rather, that this list was made, including all the names that -- of persons that you mentioned in the statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's not a document really. It's just a list of names of persons that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me now, please, you say that parallel structures were being established.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the basis of what I managed to make out on the basis your testimony, I assume that you will agree with me that it is important to place events at a given time, to put them within a time frame work; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I ask that just the identity of the participants of this meeting be given in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't think it was given in private session before. Possibly it should have been out of abundance of caution. Yes. Do you want to ask anything more about the -- about the lunch?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, I have separated the notes I took during public session and the notes I took during private session. This about the luncheon was in public session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's absolutely right. You're quite right. But now the question of the participants it's thought should be in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was my error, and we did ask that those names be redacted when I realised that the names --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There was a redaction, but no criticism of you, Mr. Milosevic, but we -- if there's anything more you want to ask about the lunch, I think we better go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I'm not going to put any questions related to names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand that this was - how should I put this? - a customary thing that was done when a guest would come to the municipality, the highest representatives of the municipality would be present at that luncheon. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I assume that this was the practice that prevailed earlier on too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if a general would come, if a minister would come, the director of a company that has business links with you coming from any part of Yugoslavia. So this was basically the way in which people communicated in Zvornik; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was this luncheon held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was during the week before the week during which the attack on Zvornik took place. I don't know the exact date. I think it was the end of March, say, the 30th, the 31st of March or the 1st of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You said here that the attack on Zvornik took place on the 8th of April.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's about a week before the attack on Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let us just get the time in order, and I'd like to put some questions to you in relation to this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was my understanding that the general maintained a pleasant atmosphere during lunch, and he said it was the task of the army to defend the people, to protect the people.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that your Crisis Staff was established on the 5th of April; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said the 6th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 6th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. The 6th of April. Is the 6th of April the date when the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina was recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really don't know these details, but I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a very well-known detail, because Bosnia-Herzegovina was recognised exactly on the day of the 6th of April, the day when Hitler bombed Belgrade on the 6th of April, 1941. It's a very well known date. You, as a high official, must have been aware of this date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew that it was that, but I wasn't aware of it being exactly that 6th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can take my word for it, and it exists in documents. So on the 6th of April, the independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina is recognised on the basis of the referendum in which the Serbs did not take part. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is well known that the -- that the referendum was organised, and I know that the Serbs obstructed the referendum.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. As a high official, did you know that in Bosnia-Herzegovina the rule was to respect and observe the positions of all three peoples, the Serbs, the Croats, and the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that this referendum was illegal because the entire Serb people, as a constituent people living in Bosnia-Herzegovina, refused to take part in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We are getting well aware from this witness's evidence which was to do with Zvornik. It was quite specific. These sound like political and constitutional arguments which are not for this witness to deal with. You can address us on it in due course. Let's deal with the witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, all the more absurd to bring witnesses here before me to testify about certain events concerning the civil war in a neighbouring state and not allowing this to be linked to the political explanations that only follow as a logical consequence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You can give your evidence in due course, but the evidence which is being given is about what happened in Zvornik, and it's being given as evidence against you. The weight of it is a matter that we'll have to consider. Now, let's go on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. All right, Mr. May. But I am trying to show precisely through this witness that the activities that the witness is testifying about coincide exactly. Of course, this is from his very own position.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the 6th of April, the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Zvornik is being established, and that is what this witness claims, and I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You can ask him why it was established, of course. That's a matter he can deal with.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can ask him, Mr. May, if something were not clear, but there's no need for me to ask him whether -- what time it is now, whether it's 10.25, because I have a big clock up there and of course I can see it's 10.25. So if it was on the 6th of April that Bosnia-Herzegovina was recognised on the basis of an illegal referendum, the Crisis Staff was established precisely to carry out this kind of illegal activity further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What are you suggesting to this witness, that the Crisis Staff was set up to pursue an illegal activity? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the entire secession of Bosnia-Herzegovina was illegal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It doesn't matter about that. What are you suggesting to the witness was happening in Zvornik on the 6th of April? Now, you seem to be making a suggestion that the Crisis Staff was set up for some purpose. What I'm trying to find out is what purpose you say it was set up for.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the Crisis Staff set up because a crisis had broken out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're asking me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. You established the Crisis Staff. There was a crisis, and then you established the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Crisis is a small word. It's a small word. We established a Crisis Staff because it was quite clear that an attack was in the offing, an attack against Zvornik, and we established a Crisis Staff to avert this attack at all costs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. All right. Sorry, I've forgotten this witness's number. Somehow I don't have it written here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think B would be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1237. Very well. 1237.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. 1237. We have stated this when you established this Crisis Staff, that is to say on the 6th of April. Now, why was there a crisis on the 6th of April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the Serbs withdrew. There were no Serbs in Zvornik. Cannons and tanks were deployed at the points I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll get to cannons and tanks later, but tell me now, since you say that the Serbs left all the municipality structures in Zvornik; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did they leave these municipal structures precisely then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they started obstructing the work already towards the end of 1991, and they got out because they thought that they should no longer live together with Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. 1237, is that an explanation or is it to be explained by the fact that they do not accept this kind of state that was proclaimed and established without their consent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They left all the municipal structures even before the international recognition of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when was the referendum held? Don't you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, you don't know that. Very well. Now, in order to save time, let us look at some other details that you referred to. You said that the group of Arkan's men was arrested in Zvornik; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they arrested in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were arrested from -- at the entrance from Karakaj into Zvornik in the part of Zvornik that is called Vidak's field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, where is Karakaj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Karakaj is an industrial zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that they were on their way - how should I put this? - to meet up at the rallying point at Hotel Jezero?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, is Hotel Jezero in Mali Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So why would they be going from Serbia to the left bank of the Drina River to go to Hotel Jezero which is on the right bank of the Drina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. They were coming from Karakaj in order to cross the bridge in the centre of Zvornik into Mali Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that these men were locals of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, no. They came from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, they came from Belgrade. Belgraders went via Zvornik from the left bank of the Drina to the right bank of the Drina to the Hotel Jezero?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They reported to the Crisis Staff in Karakaj and then they were instructed to join the units in Mali Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did they manage to get to Veliki Zvornik at all? They had to go through Mali Zvornik and the Hotel Jezero where you say their rallying point was, was in Mali Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They crossed over to Karakaj. I don't know where they crossed over to Karakaj but first they reported at the rallying point in Karakaj where they were told to report, and Karakaj is about 5 or 6 kilometres away from the town of Mali Zvornik. And then from Karakaj they set out towards Mali Zvornik. And instead of crossing the new bridge they went further on in order to cross the bridge in the centre of Zvornik which is about 2 kilometres away from the Jezero Hotel in Mali Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're just talking about different territories now. Karakaj is in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and Mali Zvornik is in Serbia. You say that they came from Belgrade, and they went via Zvornik in Bosnia-Herzegovina in order to return to Serbia and Mali Zvornik. That is what you're claiming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's what they said in their statement, that via Karakaj --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And you say that they had some knives and some wires for strangling? Are there any cases that were registered of someone being strangled by a wire in this area? Do you have a single such case registered of somebody being strangled by a wire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, this is quite well known what kind of terrible crimes were committed in this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are not talking about that now. Many crimes were committed all over Bosnia-Herzegovina, but the point is who committed these crimes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I hope that the court will establish that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's now time to adjourn. We will adjourn now. Twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was told that this other microphone should be working normally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke about the Territorial Defence in a considerable part of your testimony and in your statement. Will you tell me, please, in view of the knowledge that you obviously have about all these things, are you familiar with the decision of the Presidency of the SFRY adopted in 1986 pursuant to which the commands of armies were transformed into military zone commands and that the Territorial Defence in those zones are placed under their command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not familiar with the details, but I do know that there was this decision about command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The commands of Territorial Defence were under the command of the Presidency of the SFRY.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Under the command of the JNA, the JNA and the Territorial Defence were together. Together they constituted the armed forces which were Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. under the command of the Presidency. Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was part of the concept of All People's Defence, and they were a component part of the defence system of the SFRY; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you remember the order of the Presidency of the SFRY dated the 29th of May, 1990, that all weapons and warehouses of the TO have to be transferred to the JNA warehouses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that that order was issued precisely with the aim of avoiding the arms getting into the hands of any people who might have been prepared to use those weapons again the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't agree with your conclusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why then was this order issued?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Subsequent events showed that the order was issued so those weapons would not get into the hands of people who were not Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On what grounds do you make such an assertion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the grounds of the decision which was taken just before the war, about a month before the war. The decision of the command of the district staff of the Territorial Defence in Tuzla, Colonel Milojkovic to the effect that the weapons of the TO be distributed to two municipalities in Tuzla, Sekovici and Lopare, which are municipalities exclusively inhabited by Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So that is the basis on which you come to that conclusion. And tell me, what was the feelings of the population of the Zvornik area towards the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can only speak in my own name and in the name of the people I knew. Unfortunately, until the very last I believed in what I was taught, and that is that the JNA is the armed force of all the peoples and nationalities. However, it didn't prove to be so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, did Muslims respond to JNA call-ups for mobilisation which they were obliged to do as military conscripts of the state to which they still belonged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can really only speak about the TO and the mobilisation of citizens for the needs of the JNA was up not municipal Secretariat for National Defence, which is a different department and a different position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So you can't go into that. Very well. Tell me, and it is true that inspection was done of weapons in the JNA warehouses and that this inspection was carried out by a JNA officer and an official of Zvornik municipality who was a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was that inspection done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To see whether those weapons which had been paid for with the funds of the inhabitants of Zvornik municipality, whether those weapons were indeed in the place where they should have been.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, was this done to make sure that none of the weapons had gone missing and that they had not got into the hands of unauthorised persons or extremists of any ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was simply a routine control and check of weapons, routine checks of what was being alleged by the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, since when were these inspections carried out once a week?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since the beginning of 1992, at the request of President Pasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement page 2, fourth paragraph, you make a rather radical statement I would call it, that members of the SDS were aggressive, evil, and that they hated everything that was non-Serbian. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In making such a statement, were you referring to all of them, to all Serbs, or to all members of the SDS, or to certain individuals in the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was referring to the SDS discussions that I heard and saw with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you quoted one discussion of the SDS which doesn't speak of any kind of hatred but only about exploitation as far as I gathered. That is what you quoted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any other shall I call it a fact or argument to corroborate such an allegation of yours that they hated everything that was non-Serbian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Judging by their behaviour in the town of Zvornik itself, they were able to park, and they did park their cars wherever they wanted. No one dared protest, not even the police. They started killing Muslims, overtly advocating that Zvornik was Serbian, that it would be Serbian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come this is not mentioned in your statement that somebody started killing Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Will you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is: How is it that this -- that somebody started killing Muslims in Zvornik and that they were saying that Zvornik was Serbian is not in your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, nobody asked me about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You say that the SDS enjoyed the support of the Serbian academy of sciences, the Yugoslav state security service and the General Staff of the JNA; is that what you assert?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do assert that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could you tell me when, where, and how did these institutions or services express their support for the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember a statement on Sarajevo television by general -- a general who was then the commander of the General Staff of the Yugoslav People's Army, General Adzic, who explicitly stated the Yugoslav People's Army will defend the interests of the Serbian people. And what the interests of the Serbian people were was determined by the SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am afraid you wrongly connected things. When did General Adzic say this, and on what occasion? And was it linked to a particular event? Do you remember the context?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was one of his statements on television. I don't remember on what occasion, nor the exact date, but I do know that he said that the Yugoslav People's Army would defend the interests of the Serbian people. He said that loud and clear. Unfortunately, I didn't know you would ask me that, because I probably could have found out the exact date. There must also be recordings available.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Adzic was well known as somebody who advocated the preservation of Yugoslavia and the equality of all the Yugoslav peoples. Surely you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that, and I don't believe that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't distinguish between solidarity with the people that was in jeopardy, in this case the Serbian people, from the support of a party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is your opinion, and I think that it is not correct that anyone in Bosnia-Herzegovina were in jeopardy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But on page 7, in paragraph 1, you say that it was clear that the local Serbs didn't know that war was being prepared. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The leadership didn't know, but the most extreme section did. Ivanovic and Mijatovic didn't know that Zvornik would be attacked and that what was done would be done. That was my opinion. Otherwise, they wouldn't have agreed to a division of Zvornik municipality and the restoration of normal life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, what are you really claiming? Were the local Serbs aggressive and evil people who implemented the plans of the Serbian academy of sciences and the Yugoslav State Security Service, as you say, or did they not at all know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The most extreme section knew, and I think that Ivanovic and Mijatovic did not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. We'll come to that later, as there are certain things that were discussed in private session, and I wouldn't like us to go into private session. Tell me, please, on page 2, paragraph 6 of your statement you say at that leading positions in Zvornik were held by Serbs and that as in other places of Yugoslavia, as you put it, they were privileged. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me then who from the beginning and during all these conflicts was president of Zvornik municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A Muslim, elected at the elections.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was chief of police in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was commander of the Territorial Defence in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, then, since this is in contradiction with your statement, you yourself have just confirmed this, and you say that Serbs were privileged in the former Yugoslavia, give me at least one basis for this claim that Serbs had greater or broader rights than the rest of the Yugoslav peoples.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Eighty per cent of the positions of general managers in Zvornik were held by Serbs. Eighty per cent of the housing stock, of the socially owned housing stock was utilised by Serbs. This is an enormous, enormous economic privilege.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who appointed them to those positions? Did they appoint themselves or in Zvornik municipality in which you yourself said there were 60 per cent Muslims and 38 per cent Serbian and 2 per cent others. I took note of these figures made during your own public testimony. How could the Serbs in a system of self-management in which decisions were taken by -- in the way in which you are very familiar with, how could they have got to those positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Any important position, as you know probably very well, could not be taken without a decision by a municipal commission, a special commission which was under the control of the Municipal Committee of the League of Communists of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that the Muslims were not members of that same committee?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course. Throughout the post-war period. I'm not talking about the period after the elections and the outbreak of the conflicts, but the main say was held by the Serbs. In the Municipal Committee of the League of Communists of Yugoslavia and in the state security service. Those were two institutions which had the greatest influence regarding personnel policy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you mentioned a moment ago that both the president of the municipality and the chief of police and the TO commander were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, after the elections.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in this former state of SFRY, did anyone prevent you Muslims from practising your faith, to being educated, becoming well-known sportsmen, artists, judges, president of the Presidency of Yugoslavia, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, nobody prevented us from doing that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during that former common state of ours, was any mosque perhaps destroyed or during the existence of that Yugoslavia, were more Islamic religious buildings built than over five centuries of Ottoman rule in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know whether that was quite so, but I do know that mosques would be built without any problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also true that in the Yugoslavia such as it was at the time Muslims acquired the right to declare themselves as being members of the a Muslim nation for the first time in history?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct. The constitution of 1974, I think, envisaged that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true in the SFRY Muslims had their representatives in all the top level state and military bodies, that in every respect they participated on a footing of equality, in social, political, and every other aspect of life in SFRY?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We really cannot waste more time on this. These are all matters of history. They are not particularly for this witness to deal with. He didn't give any evidence about this, and your time must be limited, and it mustn't be wasted on peripheral matters. Now, you have, Mr. Milosevic, one hour left. We will give you that. That is longer than the Prosecution had. But you must deal with relevant matters with which this witness is concerned, not general matters.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, this witness testified for two hours and 35 minutes, according to my arithmetic. Before the break, I questioned him for 25 minutes, so please be kind enough and work out how much more time is left for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The answer is one hour. The Prosecution examined him for one hour, 40 minutes, and you can have slightly longer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That can be checked in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in the period you are testifying about, that is the beginning of January 1992, what was the only legal military organisation pursuant to the law and the constitution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Yugoslav People's Army and the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the JNA have units and barracks all over the territory of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not everywhere, because by then it had already retreated from Slovenia and the conflict was ongoing in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But was there any violation or any prohibition on JNA units being stationed in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not familiar with those details.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke of a unit which was relocated from Jastrebarsko in Croatia to the territory of Zvornik, and you marked some points where the forces of that unit were deployed of that same unit; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you call that unit a military group, don't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was an armoured mechanised brigade from Jastrebarsko, and these were parts of that brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 3, paragraph 1, however, you say that these were members of the reserve force of the JNA; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They appeared after the New Year holidays in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you, too, a member of the reserve force of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not. I was a member of the TO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in your statement, you say that they were visited daily by JNA officers and that between the JNA and the reservists there were close links, but those reservists, weren't they members of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were reservists who had been mobilised mostly -- not mostly but a hundred per cent from parts of Zvornik municipality inhabited by Serbs. They were all Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, tell me, please, was this due to the fact that Muslims already then refused to respond on the basis of the political position taken by the SDA? They did not respond to call-up papers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything in connection with the mobilisation of the Muslim police in Zvornik, and who ordered it, that is, the mobilisation of the Muslim police in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the activities in that connection by the president of the municipality and a SDA representative, Abdulah Pasic and Nedzad Pavic, later commander of the 1st Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. I hear that name for the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you respect the order issued on the 4th of April, 1992, while the B and H was still part of SFRY issued by Alija Izetbegovic to mobilise the TO, the police, and the Civil Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never heard of that order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never heard of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that on the 12th of April Izetbegovic ordered an all-out attack on barracks in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. And on page 3, paragraph 3 you refer to some activities of the JNA in that area and you say that every bridge in Zvornik was secured with some weapons of its own by the JNA and that there was several tanks around Sehovici inhabited exclusively by Serbs; that is what you say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the army deploy its units to areas where that unit was located which had come from Jastrebarsko, and then relocated to the territory of Zvornik municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it mostly relocated its forces so that Zvornik municipality should find itself surrounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know in view of all the jobs that you did that the JNA was securing communications, roads, bridges, that it was not carrying out any sort of blockade, it was doing simply the securing operation? It was not in order to control roads and bridges. It was securing them from sabotage attacks and anything else that could have been expected at the time. Was that the way it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it wasn't like that. In peacetime there is no need for any activity of the JNA that was carried out at the time in Zvornik municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From who then was the JNA protecting the bridges, Sekovici? From whom if there is no danger at all? Why would they need to secure those facilities, for what reason?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To occupy the best, the most favourable positions for attacking Zvornik later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your description, I understand that you are talking about the conflict in Zvornik itself, and you are mentioning paramilitary formations. I am not aware that it was the JNA who attacked Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The JNA did the artillery shelling together with Territorial Defence units and thus prepared the Zvornik municipality for what came later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know who Sead Hadziavdic is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know who he is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that precisely according to the reports of your security of Zvornik dating back to autumn 1991, that person dealt in the illegal arming of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you know nothing about that, do you know that the same was done in Kamenica, by Saban Redzic [phoen] and Esad Haskic [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know that either?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't. I did my job honestly and with honour, trying to be as little affiliated politically as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that doesn't mean that you couldn't have been informed about Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. what other people were doing if it was illegal and could be conducive to conflicts. On the contrary, it should have been your obligation to know that. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it should have been but I know nothing about the activities you mention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's curious, because occupying the position you occupied in Zvornik, you knew nothing about those activities, and I as a president of another state, a neighbouring state, am supposed to know about these activities. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's a comment, not for the witness to answer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. All right, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that a very important role in the arming and military organising of precisely Zvornik Muslims was played by Captain Hajrudin Mesic, former chief of police in Ugljevik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me please about Colonel Tacic. You say that he was a very able officer because he managed to retreat with his unit intact, his weaponry intact from Jastrebarsko and deploy them where he was told to. Does this observation of yours speaks to the intensity of attacks in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't mean the intensity of attacks. I knew that there were open conflicts there and attacks on JNA barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 3 in paragraph 4, you say that Colonel Tacic was often interested in facilities that the Territorial Defence of Zvornik held in Drinjaca and asked you for permission to use those facilities to accommodate soldiers. Is that true?
